rule_affected: IDENTITY_REVEAL_PROTOCOL preconditions 1-4 (freeze and SHA-256 recorded before A/B reveal)
description: The six blinded decisions were made and the A/B identity was revealed inside the working conversation, before any adjudication file existed in the workspace. The protocol requires the adjudication file to be hashed and freeze-gated before reveal. That sequence cannot be satisfied retrospectively.
action_taken: Imported as a new versioned artefact rather than as a protocol-compliant freeze, per the protocol clause requiring later administrative correction to be a new versioned artefact with justification. Blinding at decision time rests on the reviewer attestation, not on a contemporaneous hash. post_reveal_status marks every row accordingly.
effect_on_claims: The six decisions remain usable as qualitative, purposively selected human validation. They cannot be presented as a protocol-compliant frozen adjudication, and the absence of recorded justifications means the reasoning behind each decision is not auditable.

rule_affected: HUMAN_ADJUDICATION_PROTOCOL (justification and confidence are required fields on each card)
description: The external export carried card_id and decision only. No justification, confidence or per-card date was captured.
action_taken: Recorded as NOT_RECORDED. No justification was reconstructed or inferred.
effect_on_claims: Each decision is auditable as a decision but not as reasoning. Any methodological effect attributed to a decision must be stated as the reviewer’s unexplained preference between two frozen propositions.
